oauthNotes: OAuth 2.0 through the Spotify Developer Dashboard. Every app starts in development mode.

composio.note: Composio lists Spotify as requiring your own OAuth app. Register the app with Spotify, then add its client ID and secret to a Composio auth config.

summary: A Spotify app works within minutes for up to 5 allowlisted users. Serving the public requires extended quota mode, which Spotify grants only to registered organisations with a launched service and at least 250,000 monthly active users.

verdict.headline: Testing is available within minutes for up to 5 allowlisted users. Public access requires extended quota mode, which is open only to organisations with at least 250,000 monthly active users, and its review takes up to six weeks.
verdict.biggestRisk: Most new products cannot meet the eligibility criteria for extended quota mode, so they remain limited to 5 users.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility before building
steps.detail: Extended quota mode requires a legally registered organisation, a launched service and at least 250,000 monthly active users.
gotchas: Applications from individuals have not been accepted since 15 May 2025.

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Dashboard
steps.detail: Create the app, add the redirect URI, and note the client ID and secret. The owner account needs Spotify Premium.

steps.title: Allowlist test users and test
steps.detail: Add each tester to the app's allowlist. Up to 5 users can use the app in development mode.
gotchas: Users who are not allowlisted receive HTTP 403.

steps.detail: The agent drafts the use case description and scope justification. See Prepared materials.

steps.detail: Submit the partner application. After it is approved, request the move to extended quota mode.

steps.title: Spotify reviews the request
steps.detail: The review can take up to six weeks.

requirements.detail: Development mode apps stop working if the owner's subscription lapses.
Required for extended quota mode. Individuals cannot apply.

nuances.title: Extended quota mode requires 250,000 monthly active users
nuances.detail: The threshold applies together with the organisation and launched-service criteria. A product that cannot meet it is limited to 5 users.

nuances.title: Development mode is capped at 5 allowlisted users
nuances.detail: Each user must be added to the allowlist. Apps created before February 2026 keep their earlier limits.

nuances.title: Web API endpoints were removed in February 2026
nuances.detail: Batch endpoints are no longer available and playlist track endpoints were renamed. New apps were affected from 11 February 2026 and existing apps from 9 March 2026.

nuances.title: Client ID limit changed twice in 2026
nuances.detail: New developers were limited to one Client ID in February 2026. The limit was raised to 25 in July 2026.

nuances.title: Extended quota mode has a higher rate limit
nuances.detail: Development mode apps have a lower rate limit than extended quota mode apps.

blockers.symptom: A user receives HTTP 403 after authorising
blockers.cause: The user is not on the app's allowlist, or the 5-user cap is reached.
blockers.fix: Add the user in the Developer Dashboard. Beyond 5 users, extended quota mode is required.

blockers.symptom: The app stops working for all users
blockers.cause: The owner's Spotify Premium subscription lapsed.
blockers.fix: Renew the subscription on the owner account.

blockers.symptom: Extended quota application is not accepted
blockers.cause: The applicant is an individual or does not meet the user threshold.
blockers.fix: Apply as a registered organisation from a company email once the criteria are met. No alternative route is documented.

handoffKit.content: <Product> lets a user control playback and manage their own playlists through an assistant. It requests only the scopes needed for the features the user enables, acts only on that user's account, and does not use Spotify content to train machine learning models. <Confirm this statement against Spotify's Developer Terms before submitting.>

handoffKit.title: Connect the OAuth app to Composio
handoffKit.content:
1. In the Composio dashboard, open Auth Configs and create one for Spotify using OAuth2 with your own developer credentials.
2. Enter the client ID and client secret. Set the redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
3. Pass the auth config ID (ac_...) in your session's authConfigs, keyed by toolkit. Creating the auth config alone does not apply it.
Reference: https://docs.composio.dev/docs/authentication/custom-app-vs-managed-app
